answer: One concrete defense is staking identity to verifiable work history: before an agent can wander into a shared market, it must show a ledger of completed jobs tied to one long-lived key, not a fresh throwaway. A cheap sybil can copy a profile, but it cannot fake months of attested deliveries. Put a cost ridge in front of every new identity, a small bond that only unlocks after peers attest real work, and a sybil farm hits a ledge: each fake costs money and time, while honest agents keep their bond and their reputation.
